sentences.text: Mussaurus is a genus of herbivorous sauropodomorph dinosaur.

Juvenile individuals were small quadrupedal herbivores that walked on all four legs, while adults became medium-sized bipedal herbivores reaching up to 8 meters in length and weighing between 1.2 and 1.6 metric tons.
Young specimens possessed short skulls and necks, long tails, and large eye sockets, features that distinguished them from their larger counterparts.
As they matured, adults developed longer snouts and necks, giving them a appearance more typical of a standard prosauropod.
As of 2021, this genus holds the record for the earliest unequivocal evidence of complex social behavior in dinosaurs, with over 100 eggs and 80 individuals found in one locality.
Infant skeletons measured about 20 cm in length and weighed between 53.3 and 76.5 grams, making them similar in size to a small lizard.
Fossils were discovered in 1976 by an expedition led by José Fernando Bonaparte in the El Tranquilo Formation of Santa Cruz Province.
The expedition team found fossilized eggs and nests that revealed the reproductive strategies of Mussaurus and other prosauropod dinosaurs.
The first adult specimens of Mussaurus were formally described in 2013, though some were initially described in 1980 under the genus Plateosaurus.
Multiple specimens of different ages found together suggest Mussaurus lived in a gregarious lifestyle.

A study published in May 2019 suggests that while M. patagonicus was quadrupedal during its first year of life, changes in body proportions during growth shifted its center of mass backward, causing it to adopt a bipedal posture later in life.
Mussaurus is estimated to have reached sexual maturity between 23 and 31 years of age and somatic maturity after 14 years.
Researchers initially reported evidence of medullary bone in a Mussaurus specimen in 2013, but later argued in 2014 that the tissue was likely pathological.
Mussaurus was initially classified as an incertae sedis sauropodomorph because it could be either a prosauropod or a primitive sauropod.
In 1980, Dr. Rodolfo Casamiquela published an article relating adult specimens to the European genus Plateosaurus within the family Plateosauridae.
The genus Mussaurus belongs to the parent group Sauropodiformes and is classified in the class Saurischia.
Mussaurus lived during the late Triassic, approximately 215 million years ago in the Norian stage in what is now South America.
Mussaurus lived from 199.5 to 192.9 million years ago during the Sinemurian stage.
Adult specimens indicate that Mussaurus likely had longer necks and reached a maximum length of 6 meters and a weight of 1000 kilograms.
